cards.text: It's spring, the time when kings march out to war. David sends out Joab, the commander of his army (2 Samuel 8:16), with the whole army of Israel. They destroy the Ammonites and lay siege to the city of Rabbah.

cards.question: The whole army of Israel is out at Rabbah. So where's King David?

cards.text: The whole army is off at war, and one evening David is just getting up from his bed to stroll around on the palace roof. From up there he sees a woman bathing, a very beautiful woman.

cards.question: True or false: David sends someone to find out who the woman is.
David is told her name: Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam. Then he's told one more thing about her. What is it?

answers.text: She's the wife of Uriah the Hittite
She's a servant in the palace

cards.text: Even so, David sends messengers to get her, and when she comes to him, he sleeps with her. She had just purified herself from her uncleanness, and then she returns home.

cards.question: Some time later, Bathsheba sends word to David. What's her news?

cards.text: David sends orders to Joab: 'Send me Uriah the Hittite.' When Uriah arrives, David asks how Joab, the troops and the war are doing, like a boss making small talk in the hallway.

cards.question: Then David has a word for Uriah. He tells him, 'Go down to your ___ and wash your feet.'

cards.text: So Uriah leaves the palace, and a gift from the king follows him out. A gift from the KING, friend, and all I ever got in the junk drawer was a dusty takeout menu.

cards.question: Uriah has left the palace. Where does he sleep that night?

answers.text: At the palace door with the servants
At home in his own house
In a tent outside the city

cards.text: Then David is told, 'Uriah did not go home.' So the king asks him, and I bet he's nervous now, 'Haven't you just arrived from a journey? Why didn't you go home?'

cards.question: Uriah has an answer for the king. Why won't he go home?

answers.text: Joab and the soldiers are camped in the field
He's afraid of what the king might do
He has to leave for Rabbah at dawn

cards.question: True or false: Uriah tells David the ark is resting safely inside a house.

cards.text: Then Uriah swears, 'As surely as you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do such a thing!' The man gets a free night in his own bed and turns it DOWN, friend, and me, I have never once turned down the snooze button.

cards.question: True or false: after hearing Uriah's answer, David sends him straight back to the battle that same day.

cards.text: Uriah stays in Jerusalem that day and the next, and David invites him to eat and drink with him. Then the king of Israel gets his own soldier DRUNK, friend, I'm not making this up.

cards.question: True or false: that evening, drunk, Uriah finally goes home to his house.

cards.text: The next morning, David writes a letter to Joab and sends it with Uriah. The letter goes to the front in Uriah's own hands.

cards.question: What does David's letter tell Joab to do with Uriah?

answers.text: Put him at the front of the fiercest battle
Send him home to his wife for a while
Make him a commander over the army

cards.question: True or false: in David's letter, the plan is for the other soldiers to pull back and leave Uriah there.

cards.text: As Joab besieges the city, he puts Uriah where he knows the strongest enemy soldiers are. Joab got the letter, friend, and Joab follows the letter.

cards.question: The men of the city come out and fight against Joab. What happens to Uriah?

cards.text: Some of David's servants fall too. Then Joab sends David a full account of the battle and gives the messenger instructions, like a manager prepping you before you walk into the big boss's office.

cards.question: Joab warns the messenger that the king's anger may flare. What does Joab expect David to ask?

answers.text: Why they got so close to the wall
Why they left the ark behind

cards.text: Joab even expects David to bring up Abimelech, a son of Gideon (Judges 8:31), who died when a woman dropped an upper millstone on him from the wall in Thebez. Joab didn't just send a report, friend, he sent a report, a SCRIPT, AND the king's lines!

cards.question: If the king asks all that, the messenger has one line ready: 'Your servant ___ the Hittite is dead as well.'

cards.text: The messenger tells David everything: the enemy came out, Israel drove them back to the gate, then archers shot from the wall and some of the king's servants were killed. He doesn't even wait for the king to ask, friend, he just drops it: 'And your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.'

cards.question: David hears the news about Uriah. What message does he send back to Joab?

answers.text: Don't let this matter upset you
You were careless with my men
Pull back from the city at once

cards.text: That anger Joab warned about never shows up, friend. David just says, 'Do not let this matter upset you, for the sword devours one as well as another,' and then, 'Strengthen your attack against the city and demolish it.'

cards.question: True or false: when Bathsheba hears that her husband is dead, she mourns for him.

cards.text: When the time of mourning is over, David has her brought to his house, and she becomes his wife and bears him a son.

cards.question: One last line closes the passage: 'But the thing that David had done was ___ in the sight of the LORD.'

cards.text: I bet David thinks it's all buried, but the LORD saw it. And friend, this story is far from over.
